what_its_for: Naratriptan is used to treat migraine headaches in adults. It helps relieve the pain, nausea, and sensitivity to light and sound that come with a migraine. It is NOT used to prevent migraines or treat other types of headaches like tension headaches or cluster headaches.
how_to_take: Take naratriptan by mouth with a full glass of water. You can take it with or without food. Take it as soon as you notice your migraine starting. If your headache goes away and then comes back, you may take a second dose at least 4 hours after your first dose. Do not take more than 2 tablets in a 24-hour period. If your first dose does not help at all, do not take a second dose for the same migraine attack — call your doctor instead.
dosing: The usual starting dose is 1 mg or 2.5 mg taken by mouth at the first sign of a migraine. If needed, a second dose may be taken at least 4 hours after the first dose. Do not take more than 5 mg (two 2.5 mg tablets) in any 24-hour period. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on how you respond and your kidney or liver health.
missed_dose: Naratriptan is only taken when you have a migraine — it is not taken on a regular daily schedule. There is no 'missed dose' to worry about. Simply take it when your next migraine begins, and follow the dosing instructions as directed.
storage: Store naratriptan at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medication safely — ask your pharmacist about a medication take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking naratriptan within 24 hours of using another triptan medication (such as sumatriptan or rizatriptan) or an ergotamine-type medication (such as Cafergot or Migranal). Avoid alcohol while taking naratriptan, as it can worsen headaches and side effects. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery if you feel drowsy or dizzy after taking this medication. Do not take naratriptan if you have heart disease, a history of stroke, uncontrolled high blood pressure, or certain types of migraines (such as hemiplegic or basilar migraine) without talking to your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: chest pain, tightness, or pressure; pain or tightness in your jaw, neck, or throat; shortness of breath; severe stomach pain; sudden severe headache different from your usual migraine; weakness or numbness on one side of your body; slurred speech; vision changes; fast or irregular heartbeat; signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, swelling of your face or throat, or difficulty breathing. Also call your doctor if your migraines are not getting better, if you need to use naratriptan more than 10 days per month, or if you have any unusual side effects.
when_it_works: Naratriptan typically begins to relieve migraine pain within 1 to 3 hours after taking it. It may work more slowly than some other migraine medications, but it tends to have fewer side effects and a lower chance of the headache coming back. If you have no relief after your first dose, do not take a second dose — contact your doctor for guidance.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Talk to your doctor before using naratriptan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Use only if clearly needed. Breastfeeding: It is not known if naratriptan passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding while taking this medication. Children: Naratriptan is not approved for use in patients under 18 years of age. Elderly (over 65): Use with caution. Older adults may be more sensitive to the effects and are more likely to have heart or blood vessel problems. Kidney or Liver Problems: If you have mild to moderate kidney or liver disease, your doctor may lower your dose. Naratriptan should NOT be used if you have severe kidney or liver disease.
